RELEASE: Friedman Raises the Roof at Association of Women in Architecture Panel | Representative Laura Friedman Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-4176 Email Me Address:  1517 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   RELEASE: Friedman Raises the Roof at Association of Women in Architecture Panel Image August 26, 2026 Press Release Highlighted work on housing reform, start on Glendale Design Review Board Above: Rep. Friedman speaks to a crowd of architects.   LOS ANGELES, CA — U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) sat down for a conversation with members of the Association for Women in Architecture + Design (AWA+D) on the topics of the Congresswoman’s housing policy and work in the Assembly on housing and land use reform. The conversation was moderated by Staci Nesbitt and Renee Dake Wilson. “I appreciate the Association for Women in Architecture + Design’s work to bring us all together for a night of productive conversations about the future we see to house more Angelenos,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30). “Housing is the crisis of our time, and everybody can play an important part in finding solutions for this issue, including our local architects. In Congress, I’m proud to co-lead House Democrat’s Housing Affordability Working Group, where we’re building towards a future where Americans can afford to put a roof over their heads.”  Prior to Congress, Friedman began her career in public service, which started in housing policy on the City of Glendale’s Design Review Board, where she served as a commissioner and as chairperson.  Friedman has spent much of her first term laser focused on cutting the red tape around building housing and lowering prices for families. She was recently selected to lead the House Democrats' Housing Affordability Working Group  by Leader Hakeem Jeffries. Language from her Cut Red Tape for Housing Act   to eliminate costly red tape around urban infill projects was included in the bipartisan 21 st  Century ROAD to Housing Act that became law in July 2026. RELEASE: Rep. Friedman Joins Protect Our Care in Burbank, Condemns Trump and Congressional Republicans for Skyrocketing Health Care Costs | Representative Laura Friedman Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-4176 Email Me Address:  1517 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   RELEASE: Rep. Friedman Joins Protect Our Care in Burbank, Condemns Trump and Congressional Republicans for Skyrocketing Health Care Costs Image August 11, 2026 Press Release Demands the Senate immediately take up the House-passed bill restoring the ACA tax credits Above: Friedman joins health care providers and advocates at McCambridge Park in Burbank. BURBANK, CA — Today, August 11, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) joined Protect Our Care, local physicians, and health care advocates at McCambridge Park in Burbank to condemn Trump and Congressional Republicans for skyrocketing health care costs across California. Friedman and the speakers highlighted how Republicans cut more than $1 trillion from Medicaid and let the Affordable Care Act's enhanced premium tax credits expire to finance tax breaks for the ultra-rich. They also called on the Senate to immediately take up the House-passed bill restoring those tax credits. The event was part of Protect Our Care's "Sick of It! Fix Health Care Now" campaign. A recording of the press conference can be found here . Democrats in the House forced a vote and passed a clean, three-year extension of ACA tax credits on January 8 by a vote of 230-196. Seventeen Republicans joined every Democrat after members forced the bill to the floor over the Speaker’s objection.  “1.2 million Californians have lost their health coverage, and that didn’t happen by accident,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) . “Trump and Congressional Republicans let the ACA tax credits expire and cut a trillion dollars from Medicaid to pay for a trillion dollars in tax breaks for the ultra-wealthy. I’m proud to have helped force a vote in the House, where a bipartisan majority passed the fix seven months ago. Every day the Senate refuses to vote, more families in my district lose care they can’t replace.” THE HEALTH CARE CRISIS

WEST HOLLYWOOD, CA – Today, August 26, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) convened a panel of the region’s top transportation officials alongside U.S. Representatives Maxine Waters (CA-43), Judy Chu (CA-28), Ted Lieu (CA-36), and Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37) to examine what the 2026 FIFA World Cup revealed about Los Angeles County’s readiness to move millions of people during the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games. The panel came just weeks before Congress decides how much federal funding Los Angeles gets for the Games. The panel brought together the agencies that run public transit across the region: LA Metro Chief Customer Experience Officer Jennifer Vides , who spoke to what the agency needs to move visitors across dozens of venues over sixteen days, including the buses, operators, and storage capacity a Games-scale operation requires and the capital projects Metro is working to finish before 2028. Los Angeles Department of Transportation General Manager Laura Rubio-Cornejo , who runs the second largest municipal transportation department in the country and is delivering street and transit improvements before 2028, including an additional zero-emissions bus maintenance facility. City of Santa Monica Department of Transportation Director Anuj Gupta , who oversees the Big Blue Bus and a department of more than 470 employees in a city that will host no Olympic venues but will be the site of at least a dozen nation houses. Friedman Drops By Local Black-Owned Plant Nursery and BBQ Joint | Representative Laura Friedman Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-4176 Email Me Address:  1517 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   RELEASE: Rep. Friedman Drops By Local Black-Owned Plant Nursery and BBQ Joint Image August 4, 2026 Press Release Highlights neighborhood favorites during National Black Business Month Above: Friedman talks to Shawna Christian, owner of Tansy in Burbank. LOS ANGELES, CA  — Today, August 4, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) toured two Black-owned businesses in California’s 30 th  District to start National Black Business Month. Friedman stopped by Tansy in Burbank and Bludso’s BBQ  in Melrose to talk to the owners, operators, and staff members about the wins and challenges of operating a small business. “Small businesses go beyond providing quality services or delicious food, they give Angelenos job opportunities and reinvest in the people that make up their community like Tansy and Bludso’s,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman. “That’s why it’s important to me to make these visits and listen to their needs, so that I can advocate for them better in Congress.” Tansy   is a local Black woman-owned and family-operated plant nursery and home goods store that first opened in Burbank in 2019, and the only such store with that distinction in Los Angeles County. Owner Shawna Christian is one of five Black business owners in Burbank. Bludso’s BBQ   is a California BBQ restaurant owned by television personality, James Beard Award Winner, and two-time Steve Harvey Hoodie Award Winner Kevin Bludso. Both businesses give back to their communities. Bludso’s BBQ  runs a scholarship program to support Black students in the Compton School District where Kevin Bludso was born and raised, and Tansy hosts their Teen Titan internship program to help young girls gain skills that teach them how to run a business effectively. RELEASE: Friedman Unveils $1,031,000 Federal Investment to Strengthen Community Safety in Glendale Ahead of the 2028 Olympic Games | Representative Laura Friedman Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-4176 Email Me Address:  1517 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   RELEASE: Friedman Unveils $1,031,000 Federal Investment to Strengthen Community Safety in Glendale Ahead of the 2028 Olympic Games Image July 27, 2026 Press Release Doubles public safety camera coverage & upgrades Glendale’s Real Time Information Center, without putting the cost on local taxpayers. Above: Friedman announcing a new federal investment in community safety at the Glendale Police Department.   GLENDALE, CA  — Today, July 27, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) announced a new $1,031,000 federal investment to strengthen community safety in Glendale ahead of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games. Friedman secured the investment after Glendale officials asked for help securing these tools needed to keep the community safe as the region prepares to welcome the world and for years to come. A recording of the press announcement can be found here . The federal investment Friedman secured allows Glendale to expand and modernize its Real Time Information Center without putting the cost on local taxpayers or diverting funds from other essential city services. “Glendale came to me with a real need, I made it a priority, and I fought in Washington to get it done,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) . “Keeping our neighborhoods safe should never depend on the size of a city’s budget. This is a million dollars to help our officers respond faster, prevent crime, and protect our families, and not a cent of it comes out of the pockets of Glendale taxpayers. The Games come and go, but this investment stays. Friedman Celebrates Official Phase-Out of Paraquat After Leading the Fight to Ban It August 31, 2026 Press Release Landmark Assembly bill authored by Friedman with Dolores Huerta clears one of the nation's most toxic pesticides from California fields BURBANK, CA —  Today, August 31, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) celebrated the official phase out of paraquat in California after every manufacturer of products containing the toxic ingredient voluntarily agreed to pull them from the market. The phase-out is the direct result of legislation Friedman authored   in the California Assembly which forced state regulators to fast-track a scientific review the pesticide industry had fought for years to delay. “Today, California reasserts itself as a leader in protecting the health of its residents by eliminating the highly toxic chemical paraquat,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) . “I will continue to do everything I can to protect Americans from harmful chemicals, especially in our air, water, and soil.” HOW FRIEDMAN'S BILL FORCED THE PHASE-OUT: AB 1963 , signed into law in September 2024, required the California Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR) to complete a formal scientific reevaluation of paraquat by January 1, 2029 — dramatically faster than the department's typical pace, with some reviews dragging on for more than two decades. DPR opened the reevaluation in November 2024 and released two preliminary scientific assessments that identified harms to the thyroid system, links to birth defects, and significant risks to wildlife. Because of AB 1963, DPR’s reevaluation gave it the authority to require manufacturers to submit new studies. They set a deadline of June 5, 2026 for pesticide manufacturers(?) to fill newly-identified gaps in the agency’s human health toxicology database.
